evidence: Measured in 1 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.06% of total volatiles (0.012mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Pseudolimonene is a volatile terpene, a class of aromatic molecules that give many plants their distinctive scents. As a close relative of the familiar citrus compound limonene, it contributes to the complex, herbal, and bright aromas of various botanicals. You are most likely to encounter it when crushing the leaves of certain mint-family herbs or specialized gingers.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been reported in several fragrant plants, notably mint-family herbs like Perilla frutescens (shiso) and Nepeta racemosa (catmint).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are beginning to map the chemical profiles of lesser-known aromatic plants to understand their potential benefits and applications. For pseudolimonene, early interest centers on its presence in essential oils that show antioxidant activity, though current literature is limited to chemical screening and botanical profiling (Oxford level: no evidence found).

structure_function.statement: Pseudolimonene is being studied for its potential role in supporting cellular defense against oxidative stress.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single paper screening the essential oil of sweet ginger for radical-scavenging compounds.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether pseudolimonene contributes to the radical-scavenging abilities of the essential oils it is found in, which could eventually make it a useful natural preservative or cellular protectant if it bears out.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An in vitro assay isolating pure pseudolimonene to measure its direct radical-scavenging capacity (using DPPH or ABTS assays) compared to known antioxidants, followed by cell-culture models to assess its effect on oxidative stress markers.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Research on pseudolimonene is currently limited to chemical profiling and essential oil screening, with no formal preclinical or clinical evidence yet available.
